## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design multi-tenant observability that preserves data boundaries and privacy, a common real-world requirement in CNF platforms.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry architecture and collectors
- Per-namespace (tenant) isolation
- PII redaction and data residency considerations
- RBAC for exporters and collectors
- End-to-end validation with minimal manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: opentelemetry.io/v1alpha1
kind: OpenTelemetryCollector
metadata:
  name: tenant-collector
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  mode: deployment
  config:
    processors:
      batch: {}
      attributes:
        actions:
          - key: tenant_id
            action: upsert
            value: ${K8S_NAMESPACE}
    exporters:
      - otlp:
          endpoint: otlp-collector.central.svc.cluster.local:4317
```

- What sampling strategy would you choose to balance visibility and cost, and why?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-cluster, tenant-isolated config rollouts with dynamic proxy configuration.

## Key Concepts
- Envoy xDS dynamic configuration and Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS)
- Kubernetes CRD-based policy model per tenant with isolation
- Canary traffic shaping with weight and time-based rollout window
- Multi-cluster consistency and safe rollback mechanisms
- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical policy design at the intersection of CNF gateways, Kubernetes admission control, and SBOM-driven security. It requires translating per-tenant risk tolerances into enforceable constraints and verifying end-to-end behavior.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA integration for admission control
- Per-namespace configuration and binding
- SBOM-driven vulnerability data (CVSS) attached to images
- Rego-based enforcement logic and concise ConstraintTemplates
- End-to-end testing: apply templates, constraints, and verify allow/deny outcomes

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: CNFImageVuln
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfimagevuln
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFImageVuln
      scope: Cluster
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package cnfimagevuln
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      # image.vulns is a list of {cve, cvss}
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment";
        ns := input.review.object.metadata.namespace;
        threshold := data.namespaceThresholds[ns];
        some i;
        vul := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["image.vulns"];
        cvss := vul[i].cvss;
        cvss > threshold; msg := sprintf("CVSS %v exceeds threshold %v for namespace %s", [cvss, threshold, ns]);
      }
```
```yaml
# Constraint: Bind per-namespace threshold
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: CNFImageVuln
metadata:
  name: cnf-image-vuln-namespace
spec:
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - {key: "cnf.namespace", operator: In, values: ["default"]}
```
```yaml
# Test manifest: should fail for CVSS > threshold and pass otherwise
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-cnf
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    image.vulns: "[{\"cve\":\"CVE-2024-0001\",\"cvss\":9}]"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-cnf
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-cnf
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/cnf:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle multi-tenant overrides for temporary risk surges?
- How would you test performance impact of SBOM parsing in high-scale deployments?

## Why This Is Asked

This question assesses practical knowledge of traffic management in multi-tenant environments. It tests understanding of Istio's traffic splitting capabilities, header-based routing, and safe rollout strategies. Candidates must balance per-tenant isolation against system complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Istio traffic management**: DestinationRules define service subsets; VirtualServices handle routing rules
- **Canary deployments**: Gradually shift traffic between versions to validate changes safely

- **Weight-based traffic splitting**: Distribute traffic percentages across subsets

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-dr
spec:
  host: cnf-gateway
  subsets:
  - name: prod
    labels:
      version: prod
  - name: canary
    labels:
      version: canary
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-vs
spec:
  hosts:
  - cnf-gateway
  http:
  - match:
    - headers:
        x-tenant-id:
          exact: canary
    route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: canary
      weight: 15
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: prod
      weight: 85
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your ability to design end-to-end provenance controls for CNF environments, specifically addressing how key rotation impacts SBOM generation and policy enforcement in multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign image signing with KMS-backed keys
- SPDX SBOM generation and attestation workflows
- Kyverno policy enforcement for signature and SBOM validation
- Key rotation impact on image provenance chains
- Namespace-scoped testing strategies and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign image with KMS-backed key
cosign sign --key kms://mykms/path/to/key \
  --attachment sbom \
  registry.example.com/cnf:latest

# Generate and attach SBOM
syft registry.example.com/cnf:latest \
  -o spdx-json > sbom.spdx

cosign attest --key kms://mykms/path/to/key \
  --type spdx --predicate sbom.spdx \
  registry.example.com/cnf:latest
```

## Implementation Strategy
Deploy this solution progressively: start with image signing, add SBOM generation, implement Kyverno policies, then automate the key rotation workflow. Test in isolated namespaces before cluster-wide deployment.
